key_insight: Wearable-derived sleep and activity patterns enabled AI detection of Parkinson’s disease and showed potential to identify associated pathology; this study is not about cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: Passive wearable monitoring warrants further evaluation for Parkinson’s screening and biomarker-enriched research recruitment, but is not established as a diagnostic tool.
method: Derived sleep and activity metrics from free-living wrist accelerometry.
Trained SAM-PD to distinguish Parkinson’s disease from healthy controls and validated it externally without retraining.
Compared SAM-PD with the MDS prodromal risk score for detecting dopaminergic deficit and α-synuclein pathology.
evidence_signal: SAM-PD achieved AUROC 0.93 in the U.S. cohort (n=159) and 0.95 in an independent European cohort (n=40), with at-risk cohort AUROCs of 0.86 for dopaminergic deficit and 0.76 for α-synuclein pathology.
watch_item: Small cohorts and limited pathology-positive cases require larger, representative validation before screening implementation.
paper_title: Wearable-based sleep and activity tracking detects Parkinson's disease and associated pathological hallmarks
